system.name: CENT
system.one_liner: a CXL-enabled, GPU-free system for LLM inference using near-bank and near-memory processing units

components.name: CXL Port
components.role: interface connecting the device to the CXL switch/host

components.name: Instruction Buffer (2MB)
components.role: receives instructions transmitted from the host

components.name: Decoder
components.role: decodes instructions into micro-ops directed to PIM controllers and PNM units

components.name: PNM Units
components.role: perform operations beyond MAC (accumulation, reduction, activation) that LLMs need

components.name: Shared Buffer (64KB)
components.role: buffer used for inter-device communication and PNM data staging

components.name: Inter-Device Communication Controller
components.role: orchestrates communication between CXL devices together with the CXL port

components.name: LD/ST
components.role: load/store units bridging the decoder and PIM controllers

components.name: PIM Ctrl
components.role: PIM controller managing PIM channels (×16), converting micro-ops to DRAM commands

components.name: GDDR6-PIM
components.role: near-bank PIM memory channel executing DRAM commands

content.key_idea: A CENT CXL device receives host instructions into an instruction buffer, decodes them into micro-ops routed to 16 parallel PIM controllers (driving GDDR6-PIM banks) and to PNM units, while an inter-device communication controller and shared buffer support peer-to-peer data flow between devices.
content.reading_order: Left to right: the CXL Port receives host input, feeding the Instruction Buffer and Decoder, which fan out to PNM Units and 16 replicated PIM Ctrl/GDDR6-PIM channels at the bottom; the Shared Buffer and Inter-Device Communication Controller sit at top-right for peer-to-peer traffic.

evidence: Figure 5 shows the architecture of a CXL device.
CENT instructions are transmitted from the host to a 2MB instruction buffer in each device
The CXL device integrates 16 PIM controllers, each managing two PIM channels

summary: CENT is a CXL-enabled, GPU-free system that uses near-bank processing units inside CXL-attached memory devices to run LLM inference without expensive GPUs. Figure 5 shows the architecture of one CENT CXL device: a CXL Port feeds a 2MB Instruction Buffer, which a Decoder (with its own PC) turns into micro-ops distributed to PNM Units and to 16 parallel PIM Ctrl/GDDR6-PIM channel pairs via LD/ST paths. An Inter-Device Communication Controller and a 64KB Shared Buffer, alongside the CXL Port, support inter-device data flow and a broadcast primitive between CENT devices. An in-figure legend distinguishes black inter-device data flow, blue intra-device data flow, and orange dashed control flow.
